summary: Three of the eight Masjid Nur workflows (announcement, volunteer signup, event RSVP) show genuine, specific mosque content — "Ramadan community night - Friday after Maghrib", "Iftar setup shift / 4:30-6:30 PM shift / 2 spots open", "Fri, Mar 14 at 6:45 PM - Fellowship hall / 86 of 120 spots". The other five render acceptance-criteria prose verbatim as product copy ("This view shows editable details, current progress, and the next step before saving", "Payer, amount, privacy choice, entitlement, receipt destination, and retry/refund options are visible") instead of the actual values, so a donation-payment screen titled "Sadaqah donation receipt" with a "Payment summary" card never shows an amount, payer, or method. Content also bleeds across workflows: the event-RSVP start screen renders the AI-citation "Answer with sources" surface, the discussion-thread start screen renders the donor-visibility card plus an "Ad preference and sponsored-message beh…" card, and the discussion-thread action/complete captures are byte-identical to the search-ai-citation ones. Layout problems compound this — chip rows overlapping list rows in the payment cards, a header sliced in half behind the app bar on care-request start, and RSVP screens rendered in blue against the community's green accent.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Across this community's workflows, is it always clear what workflow and what state (start/in-progress/complete) the user is looking at?
holisticQuestionAnswers.answer: No. Announcement, volunteer-signup and RSVP action/complete states are legible — "Volunteer signup confirmed" with "You are signed up for iftar setup", "RSVP confirmed", "Members can read the Ramadan community night update in their inbox" all name the workflow and its state. But five workflows fail it. The event-RSVP start screen shows "Knowledge and search / Cited answers, source visibility, and saved digests" and an "Iftar announcement answer" — a user landing there has no way to know they are starting an RSVP. The discussion-thread start screen shows a donor-visibility card ending "...destination, and giving history are visible before saving" plus a card reading "Ad preference and sponsored-message beh…" — nothing identifies a discussion thread. The neutral-notification screens are titled "Neutral care receipt" but carry announcement-search body copy ("Search public announcement content with citations, sender, delivery timing...") over a "Payment summary" card — three different workflows named on one screen. And the complete states of donor-visibility, donation-payment, care-request and neutral-notification all say the same thing, "Masjid preference confirmed / Members see the privacy-safe update, receipt history or citation, confirmed status, current progress, and clear next step", which describes what a complete state ought to contain rather than showing it.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does the displayed text sound like real product copy describing actual Masjid Nur content, or like generic/placeholder scaffolding?
holisticQuestionAnswers.answer: Split. Where real content exists it is convincingly mosque-specific: "Ramadan community night - Friday after Maghrib", "From Masjid Admin", "Today 6:00 PM", "Iftar setup shift — Friday 4:30 PM - tables, check-in, and meal handoff", "Community iftar RSVP — Fri, Mar 14 at 6:45 PM - Fellowship hall", "Sadaqah donation receipt", "Private care request — Meal support request with public summary and protected details". But the majority of body text on the remaining screens is specification prose describing what the UI is supposed to contain rather than the content itself: "This view shows editable details, current progress, and the next step before saving", "Member-visible summary, protected details, receipt or citation, and recipient preview stay visible before sending", "Amount, payer, recipient, method, visibility, and retry/refund path are visible before checkout", "Edit, withdraw, approve, reject, request changes, reopen, or appeal actions match the state". Worse, the AI-citation screen's "Query" field reads "Member-safe update with respectful language and privacy boundaries" — which is the donor-visibility workflow's subtitle, not a search query a member would have typed.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Is the visual execution production-grade — no repeated generic shells, no clipping or crowding, consistent theming?
holisticQuestionAnswers.answer: No. The identical "Answer with sources" four-row card (Query / Public summary / Protected details / Record) is stamped on six screens across three different workflows, and the same "Payment summary" five-row card is stamped on six more, so the app reads as one template re-skinned rather than distinct surfaces. There is real clipping and crowding: on care-request start the "Public summary" heading is sliced horizontally in half by the app bar; on donation-payment start/complete and all three neutral-notification screens the chip block ("Community care", "Privacy checked", "Receipt record", "Member inbox") overlaps the top of the "Public summary" list row with no gutter; the donor-visibility and discussion-thread start screens open mid-sentence on "destination, and giving history are visible"; titles truncate as "Community discussio…", "Anonymous donor vis…", "Neutral care notificati…"; and the search-ai-citation start screen's "Update privacy" button is cut through by the bottom nav. Theming is also inconsistent: the two RSVP screens render in a blue palette (#2E77A6-ish header and cards) while every other screen and the persistent app bar use the community's green accent, and the RSVP action screen's dark navy backdrop is unlike any other modal in the set.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Are the available actions clear, and is it clear why disabled or ghosted ones are in that state?
holisticQuestionAnswers.answer: Partly. Primary CTAs are named well — "Save visibility", "Publish announcement", "Submit signup", "RSVP to event", "Submit request" — and the filled teal treatment on the modal screens makes the primary obvious. Two problems recur. First, on every modal (donor-visibility action, announcement action, volunteer-signup action, event-rsvp action) a second control sits below the primary in a dim low-contrast teal — "Update privacy", "Preview announcement", "Edit availability", "Change response" — with no visible reason for its washed-out state; it reads as disabled but is labelled as an ordinary next step. Second, the start-state CTAs ("Save visibility", "Publish announcement", "Submit signup", "Submit request") are rendered as pale outlined pills with no fill, which against the same-hue card makes them read as inert; the volunteer-signup start additionally shows two "Waiting" chips and two "Minimized" cards without explaining what is being waited on beyond "Waiting for the member form to be submitted."

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does what is shown make sense for the workflow being demonstrated?
holisticQuestionAnswers.answer: No, in five cases. The event-rsvp start screen shows the knowledge/search surface with "Iftar announcement answer" instead of an event; the discussion-thread start screen shows the donor-visibility save card and an ad-preference card; the discussion-thread action and complete captures are byte-identical to the search-ai-citation action and complete captures (verified by SHA-256: fe1bed61… and de1a59a3… each appear twice), so the discussion-thread workflow has no distinct evidence at all; the neutral-notification screens mix a "Neutral care receipt" title, announcement-search subtitle, and "Payment summary"/"Checkout and receipt" cards; and the donation-payment screens surface care-team language ("Private notes are visible only to the care team or donor account owner") on a checkout flow. Most out of place for a mosque: the card reading "Ad preference and sponsored-message beh…" with an "Open ad details" button, which appears on both donor-visibility start and discussion-thread start — sponsored-message controls are not part of any of the eight workflows under review and read as content from an unrelated community fixture.

screenReviews.critique: The screen opens scrolled mid-sentence on "destination, and giving history are visible before saving." — the workflow title is off-screen above the "Masjid Nur" app bar, so the start state never names itself. Below the four chips ("Community care", "Privacy checked", "Receipt record", "Member inbox") and an unfilled "Save visibility" pill sits a dark card reading "Community discussio…" / "Ad preference and sponsored-message beh…" with an "Open ad details" button — sponsored-message preferences have nothing to do with anonymous donor visibility at a mosque, and both its title and body are ellipsis-truncated. The lower two-fifths of the screen is empty dark green below a collapsed "Local package details" row, so the start state reads as a half-loaded page rather than an entry point.

findings.title: Acceptance-criteria sentences are rendered verbatim as user-facing copy
findings.description: Across at least fourteen screens the body text lists what the UI is supposed to contain instead of containing it: "This view shows editable details, current progress, and the next step before saving." (donor-visibility action/complete, volunteer-signup action/complete), "Member-visible summary, protected details, receipt or citation, and recipient preview stay visible before sending." (donor-visibility action, care-request start), "Payer, amount, privacy choice, entitlement, receipt destination, and retry/refund options are visible." (donation-payment action, neutral-notification action), "Amount, payer, recipient, method, visibility, and retry/refund path are visible before checkout.", "Edit, withdraw, approve, reject, request changes, reopen, or appeal actions match the state." (care-request action), and "The user sees the query, answer, citations, source visibility, and follow-up options." (search-ai-citation action) — the last written in third person about the user. The repeated strings "Member-facing text stays neutral and does not reveal sensitive care details." and "Private notes are visible only to the care team or donor account owner." appear on eight or more screens. In several cases the sentence is self-refuting: it claims an amount or assignee is visible while none is rendered.
findings.requiredFix: Replace every field-list/criteria sentence with the actual community value it describes — the amount, the private note, the assignee, the status, the query, the message body. Where no value exists for a slot, render a real empty state rather than a description of the slot.

findings.title: Donation workflow shows no amount, payer, method, or receipt on any of its three states
findings.description: All three donation-payment screens are titled "Sadaqah donation receipt" and carry a card headed "Payment summary", yet no currency figure, payer name, payment method, fund, receipt number, or transaction timestamp appears on any of them. The start screen's own subtitle promises "Amount, donor visibility, receipt destination, and giving history are visible before saving." and the action sheet asserts it twice more. The complete state is unchanged from the start state except for a clipped "Masjid preference confirmed" card, which confirms a visibility preference rather than a completed gift, so there is no evidence a payment ever occurred. The same empty "Payment summary" card is also reused as the body of all three neutral-notification screens.
findings.requiredFix: Render the real transaction on all three states: amount and currency, fund/recipient, payment method, donor visibility choice, receipt destination on start/action; and on complete, a paid badge with amount, paid-at timestamp, receipt number and a view-receipt link.

findings.title: Five workflows render another workflow's surface, and two share byte-identical captures
findings.description: The event-rsvp start screen renders the knowledge/search surface ("Knowledge and search — Cited answers, source visibility, and saved digests." plus "Answer with sources" and "Iftar announcement answer") with no event details or RSVP control. The discussion-thread start screen renders the donor-visibility save card plus an ad-preference card, with no thread, post, author, or composer. The discussion-thread action and complete captures are byte-identical to the search-ai-citation action and complete captures (SHA-256 fe1bed61f8ab… and de1a59a33d14… each appear twice in the directory), so the discussion-thread workflow has no distinct render at all. The three neutral-notification screens combine a "Neutral care receipt" title, the announcement-search subtitle, and Payment summary/Checkout cards. Four unrelated complete states share the single string "Masjid preference confirmed".
findings.requiredFix: Bind each workflow row to its own surface and re-capture: RSVP start must show the event and Going/Maybe/Not going; discussion-thread must show the thread, posts and composer across all three states; neutral-notification must show a message, sender and delivery status. Replace the shared "Masjid preference confirmed" completion string with a per-workflow confirmation.

findings.title: Sponsored-message/ad-preference card appears inside Masjid Nur
findings.description: Both the donor-visibility start and discussion-thread start screens render a dark card titled "Community discussio…" whose body reads "Ad preference and sponsored-message beh…" with buttons "Expand" and "Open ad details". Ad preferences and sponsored messaging are not part of any of the eight workflows under review and are jarring inside a mosque community surface. Both the title and body are ellipsis-truncated, so even the leaked content is unreadable.
findings.requiredFix: Remove the ad-preference/sponsored-message card from these surfaces entirely, and give any remaining minimized cards titles short enough to render without truncation.

findings.title: Headers bisected by chrome, chips colliding with list rows, and text cut off at the nav bar
findings.description: care-request start opens with the words "Public summary" sliced horizontally in half by the green app bar. On donation-payment start/complete and all three neutral-notification screens the chip block (Community care / Privacy checked / Receipt record / Member inbox) sits flush against the "Public summary" row with no gutter, the chip border touching the row icon, and wraps into a ragged 1/2/1 layout. Bottom-of-screen text is repeatedly cut mid-glyph by the Home/Calendar/Giving/Care bar: "Update privacy" on search-ai-citation start, "Member tools" on care-request start, "Saved answer" on search-ai-citation complete, "...clear next step" on care-request complete, "Volunteer signup confirmed" body on volunteer-signup complete, and the "Masjid preference confirmed" body on donation-payment and neutral-notification complete. Titles truncate as "Community discussio…", "Anonymous donor vis…", "Neutral care notificati…".
findings.requiredFix: Add bottom padding equal to the nav bar height on all scroll views, restore vertical spacing between the chip wrap and the following list rows, scroll start states to the top of their content so titles are visible, and widen or wrap card titles so they do not ellipsize.

findings.title: RSVP screens use a blue palette and offer no Going/Maybe/Not going control
findings.description: The event-rsvp action and complete screens render in blue (blue header, blue cards, navy sheet) while the Masjid Nur app bar directly above them and every other screen in the set use the community's green accent. Separately, the action screen's card headed "Choose RSVP response" explains all three options — "Going reserves a spot; maybe keeps the event visible without taking capacity; not attending releases your seat." — but renders only a single "RSVP to event" button, so the choice cannot be made. The complete screen then never states which response was recorded, and the "86 of 120 spots" capacity chip is unchanged between the action and complete states despite a confirmed RSVP.
findings.requiredFix: Re-theme the RSVP surfaces to the community green accent, render three selectable Going / Maybe / Not going controls on the action state, show the chosen response on the complete state, and decrement the remaining-spots count after a Going response.

findings.title: Same sentence printed two or three times per screen inside repeated generic card shells
findings.description: Several screens say one thing repeatedly across stacked shells. volunteer-signup complete prints "You are signed up for iftar setup with protected phone, shift time, role, and coordinator follow-up." three times (header card, "Signup record", "Volunteer signup confirmed"); event-rsvp complete prints its confirmation sentence three times; donor-visibility complete and announcement complete each print theirs twice; care-request action shows a "Public summary" heading three times. Structurally, the identical four-row "Answer with sources" card appears on six screens across three workflows and the identical five-row "Payment summary" card on six more, so distinct workflows read as one template re-skinned.
findings.requiredFix: Show each fact once, in the highest-level card that owns it, and give secondary cards distinct content (history, related records, next steps) rather than restating the headline sentence.

findings.title: Completion states carry no badge, timestamp, or resulting value
findings.description: Most complete screens can only be inferred from verb tense. announcement complete still calls itself "Announcement composer for Masjid Nur members." with no Sent badge, sent-at time, or delivery count, and offers "Preview announcement" as its only action on an already-published message. donor-visibility complete never states whether the donation ended up anonymous or attributed. donation-payment, care-request, neutral-notification and search-ai-citation complete states all share the single marker "Masjid preference confirmed", none of which matches its workflow. event-rsvp complete says "RSVP confirmed" without naming the response chosen.
findings.requiredFix: Give every complete state an explicit status badge with a timestamp and the resulting value (published at, saved as anonymous, paid, going, request #, delivered to N members), and swap pre-action CTAs for post-action ones.

findings.title: Secondary buttons rendered in near-invisible teal with no disabled explanation
findings.description: On donor-visibility action, announcement action, volunteer-signup action and event-rsvp action, a second control sits below the filled primary in a dim teal on dark-green that is barely legible — "Update privacy", "Preview announcement", "Edit availability", "Change response" respectively — and in several cases duplicates a normally-styled button already present higher on the same screen. Nothing indicates whether these are disabled or merely low-emphasis. Separately, all four start-state primaries ("Save visibility", "Publish announcement", "Submit signup", "Submit request") are unfilled outline pills on same-hue cards, reading as inert compared with the filled teal treatment the identical buttons receive on the action screens.
findings.requiredFix: Render each secondary once at an accessible contrast ratio, use the platform disabled style with an adjacent reason when a control genuinely is disabled, and give start-state primary CTAs the same filled treatment they have on the action screens.
